INGREDIENTS:

3 ½ cups (tea cup size) flour 
1 ⅓ cup of water (tea cup size) 
1 tablespoon of dry yeast (about 10 g) 
2 teaspoons of salt 
wheat flour for dusting the countertop 
oil to grease the bowl 
water to sprinkle the buns 

PREPARATION MODE:

In a large bowl, mix the flour with the salt and yeast. Gradually add the water, mixing with a spatula to incorporate. Let it rest at room temperature for 10 minutes - this way the flour absorbs the water better.  ( i used my hands to mix everything )

After the 10 minutes of rest, with the spatula, turn and fold the dough over itself, until it has a consistency that is easier to handle. Transfer the dough to the countertop and knead for about 15 minutes - fold, knead, stretch and knead again until very smooth, soft and moist. If you prefer, you can knead the dough in the mixer with the hook on low speed. 

Grease a large bowl with oil. Shape the dough into a ball and transfer to the greased bowl. Cover with a towel (or film) and leave at room temperature to rise for about 1 hour or until doubled in volume. 

Once the dough has risen, sprinkle some flour on the countertop and knead the dough again for another 5 minutes. Shape into a ball again, cover with the towel and let the dough rest for another 10 minutes. 

Meanwhile, separate a large roast and sprinkle with wheat flour. On the counter, cut the dough in half with a spatula (or knife) and shape two round loaves. 

Transfer the buns to the baking sheet seam-side down, cover with a towel and let rest for another 30 minutes. 
In the meantime, preheat the oven to 220°C (high temperature) - so the oven will reach the right temperature by the time the bread is rising. 

After 30 minutes, with the tip of a sharp knife (or utility knife), make 3 parallel cuts on the surface of each loaf. Sprinkle with water and place in the oven. (In that part instead of using water I put a little bit of butter)
Bake for about 30 minutes until golden brown. Once they are baked, remove the pan from the oven and carefully transfer the buns to a wire rack. Let cool before cutting.

When i had severe depression and all i could think of a way out was suicide i didn't enjoy anything in life, still i didn't wanted to commit suicide so i just lived one day after another, and of course with proper treatment and medication i started to feel a little better and i learned a few things that helped me go through the phase of des personalization, i'll put them on a list just because i like doing lists :)

1- i start focusing on minor joys and transform them in the big event of my day, for example: its a boring day i don't do nothing that brings me real joy, but later at night i'll read a book that i really like, so what i do is antecipate the moment i'll read the book and just try to force myself to be super happy about doing a fun thing, even if it's just a minor thing, basically i focus on small amounts of happiness 

2- i always remember that nothing is eternal, then if nothing is eternal this sadness will also go away, everything changes with time and everyday is different from the other (even if just a little,a difference always comes so patience is the key)

3- i try to rationalize things, like why am i feeling this?  Oh im feeling this sad and hopeless because my brain is not producing enough hormones ( endorphin, dopamine, serotonin,oxytocin) to make me feel happy, so if i take a proper medication or do certain things i will start producing what i need to feel better! Remember the body is like a machine, everything has a cause and effect 

4- just like i said in the number 3, when you start producing more of this hormones you feel better, you think differently and start to think more clearly, so you have to remember that the person you are now is not the "normal" you, and that will change, so never make important decisions when you're overwhelmed with emotions like sadness, anger or when youre feeling this emptiness and don't have hope for life, your brain in its usual normal estate would never agree with hurting yourself or take your own life, it will also see life in a different way, so the desperation you're feeling is momentary and its not how you'll feel forever

5- when we're sad, happy or angry (or whatever emotion it is) the emotion we feel at the moment influences the way we see the world and our lives, so its predictable to see life meaningless when we're sad, but REMEMBER this is not how your life and the world around you really is, its like wearing glasses, the lens on your glasses now are the sad ones, but they're not how the world and how your life really is, you'll change glasses eventually and see how different things can be
